mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered quarters, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered periods, or the signal fails during periods of strong wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and lowers profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when oil prices are simultaneously falling sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent surge in savings rate (proxied by RSAFS growth > 10% month-over-month) signals a liquidity trap environment, which historically coincides with muted equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal income (PAYEMS) above 0.5% for four consecutive months, without a corresponding rise in consumer spending (GDPC1 flat), suggests a savings glut that depresses demand and earnings growth, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for 4 consecutive months AND GDPC1 monthly change ≈ 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not negative in at least 60% of triggered periods, or the signal fails during periods of rising inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which typically precedes tighter monetary policy and margin compression, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of rapidly rising wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annual CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 5% for six consecutive months, coupled with a flat or declining industrial production (INDPRO), indicates a stagflationary environment that historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 5% for 6 consecutive months AND INDPRO monthly change ≤ 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when oil prices are falling sharply.
